tickets.title: A failed filler must not turn a successful lookup into a refusal
tickets.objective: FillerGate.guard()'s finally block suppresses only CancelledError, then awaits the timer task. If the filler coroutine raised (TTS hiccup, audio device, Cartesia stream), that exception replaces the tool's return value. tools_wiring catches it and builds ToolResult(data={}, error=...), which usable_results() discards, so has_supporting_evidence() is False and synthesize_grounded returns REFUSAL: the user hears "I don't know" about a fact the system successfully retrieved. Dormant until T-15 put guard() on the live path; with weather p50 2663ms and github p50 1648ms every heavy turn now crosses FILLER_THRESHOLD_MS, so the filler path runs constantly. Reproduced against committed code. gate.decide() is also dead here: zero call sites in src/, duplicating the live timer rule so a future fix can land in one copy and not the other.
acceptance: A filler player that raises leaves guard()'s return value intact: the awaited tool result is returned unchanged and the exception is logged, never propagated
A test drives guard() with a player that raises and asserts the tool's real value is returned - the existing tests all use a player that always succeeds, so this direction is currently unexercised
An integration test through tools_wiring asserts a heavy tool whose filler fails still yields a usable ToolResult (non-empty data, error None) and therefore does NOT produce REFUSAL
Cancellation semantics are unchanged: cancelling guard() still cancels the timer and still raises CancelledError to the caller, and the existing no-leak tests still pass unmodified
gate.decide() is either deleted with its export, or called by _speak_after_delay so one rule governs both paths - not left as a second unreferenced copy

tickets.title: Size the synthesis token budget for an adaptive-thinking TOOL_MODEL
tickets.objective: llm/synthesis.py pins _MAX_TOKENS = 1024 and passes no thinking parameter. On claude-sonnet-4-6 omitting thinking meant thinking off, so all 1024 tokens went to the answer. Every heavy-tool turn escalates to TOOL_MODEL per route_model(), so grounded answers on exactly the turns that carry real tool data can truncate mid-sentence. A truncated answer that loses its required fact scores missing_include in the eval, so this surfaces as an unexplained grounding failure rather than a token-budget one.

tickets.title: The scope guard covers every write path, and stops guarding the plan away
tickets.objective: settings.json registers scope_guard.sh under matcher 'Edit|Write' only, so any write performed through Bash - sed -i, a heredoc, cp, git checkout - bypasses the ticket boundary entirely. scope_guard.sh line 11 then exempts .claude/* and docs/*, which is precisely docs/tickets.json, SPEC.md and DESIGN.md: the files protocol rule 1 exists to protect are the ones the guard waves through. Its path normalisation also leaves an absolute path unchanged when the target is outside CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR, so every write to a scratch or temp directory is denied while a ticket is claimed. Finally the jq glob to regex translation appends '$' but no '^', so test() searches rather than full-matches and a path merely containing a scope prefix passes.
acceptance: The guard is reached for Bash-mediated writes, or the protocol documents in CLAUDE.md that Bash is deliberately outside the boundary and why - silent bypass is not an acceptable resting state
docs/ is no longer blanket-exempt: an edit to docs/tickets.json, docs/SPEC.md or docs/DESIGN.md is denied unless the active ticket's scope lists it
A path outside CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR is allowed rather than denied - the guard constrains work inside the repo, it does not own the filesystem
The generated regex is anchored at both ends, so 'vendor/backend/src/jarvis/cadence/x.py' does not satisfy a 'backend/src/jarvis/cadence/**' scope
A test script exercises the hook directly with representative allowed and denied paths for at least three tickets, and runs in CI

tickets.title: Ticket claims are session-scoped and carry an owner
tickets.objective: .claude/active-ticket holds a bare ticket id and nothing else, so both guards key off repo-global state with no notion of who claimed it. stop_guard.sh therefore blocks every session in the repo from stopping while any ticket is open - including a read-only observer session that claimed nothing - and offers only finish, revert, or release, none of which a non-owner may safely do. scope_guard.sh has the mirror problem: with a claim active it constrains sessions that do not own it, and with no claim at all it permits everything. Protocol rule 9 contemplates three concurrent agents in worktrees, which neither guard can distinguish.
acceptance: A claim records an owner identifier alongside the ticket id, written when the ticket is claimed
stop_guard.sh blocks only the session that owns the claim; a session that owns no claim stops without being blocked
scope_guard.sh applies a ticket's scope only to the owning session
Guards behave safely when no claim exists: a missing active-ticket does not silently disable the scope boundary for a session that does hold work
A test exercises both guards for owner and non-owner sessions and runs in CI
tickets.verify: bash scripts/tests/run_claim_tests.sh
non_goals: No change to the one-ticket-at-a-time rule

tickets.title: A skipped check is never a passing check
tickets.objective: scripts/smoke_deploy.sh degrades to success when its hardest check cannot run: SKIPs do not affect the exit code, so with flyctl unauthenticated the worker-registration check skips and the script exits 0 having verified only the web process - the component the ticket is about goes unchecked while the gate reads green. T-9's own commit describes the adjacent failure, that a crash-looping machine still reports state started, so a machine-state check could not see the OOM. The same shape appears in tests/memory/conftest.py, where require_db calls pytest.skip when Postgres is unreachable: the memory integration suite vanishes with no failure, and a green run means two different things depending on the machine.
acceptance: smoke_deploy.sh exits non-zero when a check could not be performed against a target that is supposed to be deployed - unrunnable is a failure, not a pass
The worker check verifies the worker is serving rather than merely present: a crash-looping or capacity-starved machine does not satisfy it
A run with no credentials and a run against a healthy deployment are both covered by a test of the script's own exit-code logic
The memory suite's skip is loud: a run where the database was unreachable cannot be reported as a clean pass, and the summary states which suites were skipped
docs record which checks require which credentials, so a green local run's meaning is unambiguous

tickets.title: T-19's verify can actually fail, and no verify string can neuter itself
tickets.objective: T-19's pinned verify ends "--client echo || true": shell left-associativity makes the whole command exit 0 even when its pytest leg fails, and the inner eval leg genuinely exits 1 at HEAD (the echo client mirrors each fixture, tripping exactly 10 content guards against --max-fabrications 0 -- a known, stable outcome the pinned string discards). Confirmed still true after the T-17..T-27 batch: the chore that fixed T-23's string left T-19's untouched, and T-24's enumeration documented the neutering without repairing it (a deliberate no-retroactive-edit choice recorded in its completion commit).
